description: Tacos al Pastor are a vibrant Mexican culinary delight, featuring thinly sliced pork marinated in a rich blend of chiles, achiote, and pineapple. Traditionally cooked on a vertical spit, the meat is shaved off and served in warm tortillas with fresh toppings. This iconic dish captures the heart of Mexican street food culture.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chiles
instructions.text: Rehydrate guajillo and ancho chiles by simmering them in hot water for 15-20 minutes until softened. Drain and reserve a little soaking liquid for the marinade.

instructions.title: Make the Marinade
instructions.text: In a blender, combine the rehydrated chiles, achiote paste, white vinegar, pineapple juice, garlic, ground cumin, dried Mexican oregano, ground cloves, salt, and the small piece of white onion. Blend until very smooth, adding a little reserved chile water if needed to achieve a thick paste consistency.

instructions.title: Marinate the Pork
instructions.text: Thinly slice the pork shoulder into 1/4-inch thick pieces. In a large bowl, coat the pork thoroughly with the prepared marinade. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to deeply meld.

instructions.title: Assemble the Spit
instructions.text: If using a vertical spit (trompo), stack the marinated pork slices onto the spit, alternating with pineapple rings. Place a larger pineapple slice on top to secure the meat. If using a horizontal rotisserie, thread the pork onto the spit, ensuring it is tightly packed.

instructions.title: Spit Grill the Pork
instructions.text: Preheat your grill or oven with a rotisserie attachment to medium-high heat (around 350-375°F or 175-190°C). Cook the pork on the spit, rotating slowly, for 30-45 minutes, or until the edges are nicely caramelized and the internal temperature reaches 145°F (63°C). Baste occasionally with any remaining marinade or pineapple juice.

instructions.title: Shave and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, carefully shave thin slices of the caramelized pork directly from the spit using a sharp knife. Warm the corn tortillas on a comal or skillet until pliable. Fill each tortilla with the shaved al pastor meat, then top with finely diced white onion, fresh cilantro, and a generous squeeze of lime juice. Serve immediately.

instructions.title: Optional Finishing Touch
instructions.text: For an even richer flavor and crispy texture, you can quickly sear the shaved al pastor pork on a hot griddle or cast-iron pan for a minute or two after removing it from the spit, before assembling the tacos.

tips: For the most authentic flavor, use a vertical spit (trompo) if possible. If not, a horizontal rotisserie or even baking in an oven with occasional turning can work, though the texture will vary.
The quality of your dried chiles greatly impacts the marinade flavor. Always rehydrate them thoroughly and blend until the marinade is incredibly smooth for the best result.
Serve your tacos immediately after assembling to enjoy the warmth of the tortillas and the freshness of the toppings. A side of salsa verde or salsa roja is always a welcome addition.
